module_title: Important Internet Protocols - Foundational Basics and Full Forms
introduction: A 'Protocol' is simply a standard 'Set of Rules' that determines how data is transmitted between different devices in the same network. Without protocols, computers wouldn't understand each other. At this level, we focus on the most commonly tested full forms and primary functions of everyday internet protocols.

core_concepts.title: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol / Internet Protocol)
core_concepts.description:
The foundational underlying protocol suite of the entire Internet. 
- TCP's job: Breaks down large data into smaller, manageable 'Packets' before sending, and reassembles them at the destination.
- IP's job: Adds the correct destination 'Address' to each packet so it routes to the correct computer.

core_concepts.title: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)
core_concepts.description: The foundation of data communication for the World Wide Web (WWW). Whenever you type a website address in a browser (like Chrome), HTTP is the protocol used to fetch the webpage from the web server and display it on your screen.

core_concepts.title: FTP (File Transfer Protocol)
core_concepts.description: A standard network protocol used strictly for the transfer of computer files between a client and server on a computer network. It is used when you 'Upload' or 'Download' heavy files to a server.

core_concepts.title: Email Protocols: SMTP vs. POP3
core_concepts.description:
Email uses different rules for sending and receiving:
- SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol): Used strictly for 'Sending' or 'Pushing' emails from your outbox to the email server.
- POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3): Used strictly for 'Receiving' or 'Pulling' emails from the server down to your local computer/inbox.

important_entities.name: HTTPS
important_entities.significance: The 'S' stands for 'Secure'. It means all communication between your browser and the website is encrypted. Banking and shopping websites strictly use HTTPS to protect your passwords.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants often get confused by the number '3'. It simply denotes 'Version 3' of the protocol. The core name is just 'Post Office Protocol'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: The S and P Email Rule
mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: S for Send (SMTP), P for Pull (POP3)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use SMTP to Send/Push the mail away. Use POP3 to Pull/Retrieve the mail to you.

exam_strategy_tips: SSC Tier-1 exams frequently ask for the full expansion of these acronyms. Memorize 'Simple Mail Transfer Protocol' perfectly, as examiners will try to trap you with options like 'System Mail Transfer' or 'Simple Message Transfer'.
